notes: files[].content is UTF-8 text; files[].contentBase64 is raw bytes.
synthesize[] appends count files: {n} in pathPattern is the zero-based index as five decimal digits, and each file holds size bytes of value fill, with mode 100644 unless mode is given.
files[] come before synthesized files; input order never changes a digest.

files[].type is the entry kind an archive reader or walker reports: file (the default), fs-hardlink and reparse-other are read as regular files; symlink, archive-hardlink, reparse-name-surrogate, reparse-af-unix, reparse-wsl, device, fifo, socket and cont (tar type '7') fail with tree.unsupported_entry; directory and pax-global (a PAX 'g' header) add nothing to the tree but count toward the entry limit. A directory entry name must pass the path and segment rules but gets no NFC check; it may end with one '/', which is not part of its path, and '//' is unsafe. A pax-global name is metadata and is not checked.
An entry is a header that Go archive/tar Reader.Next returns. PAX 'x' and GNU long-name headers fold into the following entry and never appear in files[].

A directory, symlink or reparse-name-surrogate entry whose own name is a noise directory name is noise and is dropped without being followed. A non-directory entry of any type whose own name is a noise file name is noise; a directory with such a name is an ordinary directory.

A directory entry also takes part in the file-versus-directory check: a file equal to a directory entry path is tree.unsafe_path, and one equal under case folding is tree.case_collision. Directory entries are compared only with files, never with each other or with implied directories. A directory that a walker presents is a directory entry too, given without a trailing '/'; so an empty walked directory 'a' next to a file 'A' is tree.case_collision.
A pax-global entry whose paxRecords include path, linkpath, size or any GNU.sparse.* key fails with tree.unsupported_entry. Global records never apply to other entries.
files[].headerMode, when present, is the raw tar header mode in octal and replaces mode: the type bits (0o170000) are removed and the rest must be exactly 0644 or 0755.
type tar-nul is an old-style tar type NUL entry: a regular file, or a directory when its name ends with '/'. No other type is reclassified by a trailing '/'; a file entry 'refs/' is tree.unsafe_path.

files[].rawPathBase64, when present, replaces path with raw name bytes. Names that are not valid UTF-8 (including an unpaired UTF-16 surrogate, given as its WTF-8 bytes) fail with tree.unsafe_path; zip names are judged the same way whatever their UTF-8 flag says.
synthesize[].type, when present, sets the entry type of every synthesized entry.
A segment that starts with .ak-tmp. fails with tree.unsafe_path. Segment lengths count UTF-8 bytes, and paths sort by UTF-8 bytes, never by UTF-16 code units.
tree.read_failed has no vector: it depends on a read error, not on entry data.
files[].paxRecords, when present, are the PAX records of that archive entry.

Vectors model archive reading: the total entry limit counts every entry in files[] and synthesize[] of any type, including directory, pax-global, rejected types and noise; the tree root is not an entry; the file limit counts regular-file entries only.

files[] and synthesize[] are the entries the input presents. An archive presents every entry, noise included; a directory walker presents noise files it visits but prunes noise directories without presenting their contents.
Case collisions compare NFD(fold(NFD(path))) with full case folding (CaseFolding.txt statuses C and F), for files and for every directory prefix.
Vectors with expect.error must fail with exactly that code; no digest is defined.

Walker conformance materializes each vector as a directory: every non-directory entry becomes a file at its path with its bytes (or the item its type names), every directory entry and every parent of a path becomes a directory, and the walker walks the result, never listing a pruned noise directory or a directory whose own path is unsafe. Each directory it walks counts as one entry. A vector whose entries the host cannot create (devices, case-colliding or reserved names, invalid names on Windows) is skipped on that host.

files[].mode other than 100644 and 100755 is a tar header or git index mode. A walker maps permission bits instead and never rejects them: any execute bit gives 100755, otherwise 100644. On a host without modes (Windows), walker runs skip positive vectors that contain 100755.

archiveOnly: true marks a vector that binds archive readers only, and walker conformance skips it: one with more than one defect (more than one validation step fails on its own), one with no on-disk form (an archive-only type or field, an empty, '.' or '..' path segment, a NUL, a segment over 255 UTF-16 code units, a file mode other than 100644, 100755 or 120000, two entries with one path, or a file whose path is also a directory), one that tests archive entry counting (limit-entries-count-noise), or one whose materialized walk gives a different result, such as an entry count that the walked parent directories change.
A positive vector without expect.serialization defines only the digest.
